title: Multimodal digital biomarker for asthma: complementary roles of vocal, clinical and demographic factors
desc: Asthma affects over 260 million people worldwide, yet diagnosis remains dependent on spirometry and specialist assessment, limiting accessibility in primary care and low-resource settings. Vocal biomarkers offer a promising non-invasive alternative, but prior studies have largely focused on acoustic features without integrating clinical context. We present a multimodal Mixture-of-Experts framework for asthma identification that adaptively combines acoustic embeddings from sustained vowel phonation and reading passage tasks with structured clinical and demographic data. The model was evaluated on a matched cohort of 1218 self-reported asthma cases and healthy controls from the Colive Voice study. The multimodal model achieved an AUROC of 0.83 and Brier score of 0.18, outperforming unimodal approaches. Exploratory analysis of the gating mechanism in asthma cases showed that greater respiratory symptom burden was associated with increased weighting of reading-passage modality and reduced weighting of sustained-vowel phonation modality. These findings support the feasibility of voice-based identification of self-reported asthma; however, independent prospective validation remains necessary before clinical use.

title: Liquid biopsy and cancer therapy: current technology, diagnosis, prognosis, and cancer treatments.
desc: [Molecular biomedicine] Liquid biopsy offers repeated, minimally invasive molecular profiling of cancer, but its clinical value depends on the analyte, analytical platform, and intended use. In this Review, we evaluate current liquid-biopsy technologies for diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment guidance, with a particular emphasize on tumor-derived extracellular vesicles (TDEVs) as a bridge between biomarker detection and therapeutic intervention. We examine genomic and epigenomic profiling, single-cell and single-vesicle analysis, and multi-omics integration as complementary approaches for assessing tumour burden, heterogeneity and treatment response. Circulating tumor DNA genotyping guides targeted therapy in selected advanced cancers, whereas many early-detection and vesicle-based applications require prospective validation. We highlight how the TDEV lipid bilayer protects diverse molecular cargo that reflects evolving tumour phenotypes and how TDEV-mediated communication contributes to metastasis, immune evasion and therapeutic resistance, creating opportunities to target pathogenic vesicle signalling. We also assess engineered vesicles from malignant and non-malignant cells as drug-delivery and cancer-vaccination platforms, while noting that tumour-derived carriers may retain oncogenic or immunosuppressive cargo. Most candidate vesicle biomarkers remain supported by retrospective studies, and therapeutic platforms are largely preclinical or in early clinical testing. We discuss the requirements for clinical translation, including reliable identification of tumour-derived vesicles, standardized workflows and prospective multicentre validation for diagnostics, and reproducible manufacturing, cargo characterization, potency testing and product-specific pharmacokinetic and safety evaluation for therapeutics. Finally, we consider how multimodal profiling and artificial intelligence might improve signal integration, and argue that clinical adoption will depend on demonstrating that vesicle-guided decisions and interventions improve patient outcomes.

Artificial Intelligence-Guided Precision Nanomedicine: Bridging Delivery Barriers, Controlled Release, and Clinical Translation.
desc: [International journal of nanomedicine] Targeted drug delivery aims to enhance therapeutic efficacy while minimizing systemic toxicity, yet its clinical translation remains limited by the unpredictable in vivo behaviour of nanocarriers. Although a broad range of nanocarrier platforms-including lipid-, polymer-, protein-, inorganic- and biomimetic-based systems-can improve drug solubility, pharmacokinetics, lesion-site accumulation and controlled release, their performance is frequently constrained by heterogeneous disease biology, insufficient tissue penetration, premature clearance, immune recognition and manufacturing variability. Artificial intelligence (AI) is emerging as a powerful strategy to address these multidimensional challenges. Machine learning, deep learning and computational modelling can support prediction of formulation-property relationships, release kinetics, nano- bio interactions, pharmacokinetics, biodistribution, toxicity and patient-specific therapeutic responses. In this Review, we propose an integrated, AI-guided framework that connects rational nanocarrier design, biological-fate prediction, controlled-release engineering and clinical translation within a single development pipeline. We further articulate a "translation-by-design" principle and the concept of minimum sufficient complexity, which together distinguish this Review from earlier surveys that address these stages separately. Finally, we examine key translational barriers-including data standardization, model interpretability, scalable manufacturing, safety assessment, regulatory uncertainty and the gap between preclinical efficacy and clinical outcomes-and propose that future targeted nanomedicine should move beyond increasingly complex carrier architectures toward predictive, interpretable and clinically validated AI-integrated development pipelines. Despite these capabilities, most reported models are validated on internal or closely related data; independent external and prospective validation-the evidence required before a prediction can reliably influence formulation, manufacturing or patient-level decisions-remains the principal gap in the field.

From eminence to evidence to intelligence-based medicine: optimising artificial intelligence to disrupt dogma in emergency departments.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] The evolution of medical epistemology from the unassailable authority of eminence to the empirical rigour of evidence has prepared the healthcare system for its most profound transformation yet, intelligence-based medicine. Driven by the integration of artificial intelligence (AI), this emerging era offers unprecedented capabilities to process complex health data and personalise patient care within high-stakes environments like emergency departments. However, this paradigm shift simultaneously introduces a critical risk of modernised, digital dogma, manifesting as algorithmic paternalism. If AI systems are deployed without rigorous oversight, they threaten to silently amplify historical biases, diagnostic inaccuracies, and outdated clinical heuristics, trading the unquestioned authority of historical figures for the presumed infallibility of machines. To safeguard care in emergency departments, AI must not operate unchecked. Adapting existing Learning Health System frameworks offers a pragmatic solution to govern AI integration. By embedding these computational technologies within continuous, self-correcting clinical ecosystems, departments can enforce robust data hygiene and rigorously audit data provenance. An essential component of this approach is separating objective safety surveillance and adverse event reporting from the algorithm's internal learning mechanisms to detect epistemic drift and automation bias. Ultimately, the successful and safe integration of intelligence-based medicine depends on an unwavering commitment to transparent governance. When computational power is harnessed as a regulated, transparent tool within an LHS, AI can actively dismantle entrenched clinical dogma, ensuring future care is anchored in dynamic, validated evidence rather than perpetuating the medical errors propagated by eminence from the past.

We aimed to construct the pathomics prognostic score GlyPath-Risk and explore the molecular states associated with the high-risk phenotype captured by the score. We integrated H&E whole-slide images from TCGA-PAAD and Fujian Medical University Union Hospital (FMUUH), extracted handcrafted and deep-learning features using CellProfiler and an ImageNet-pretrained ResNet-50, and constructed GlyPath-Risk using a combined LASSO and random survival forest model. Recent advances in optical coherence tomography for glaucoma: from macular imaging and optical coherence tomography angiography to artificial intelligence and portable platforms.
desc: [Current opinion in ophthalmology] Recent advances are extending optical coherence tomography (OCT)'s role beyond conventional structural metrics. This review summarizes recent developments in macular OCT, OCT angiography (OCTA), artificial intelligence (AI), and portable/home-based OCT. Macular ganglion-cell measures (ganglion-cell-inner plexiform layer, ganglion cell complex) increasingly complement retinal nerve fiber layer assessment, offering greater diagnostic/prognostic value in advanced glaucoma, myopia, and certain glaucoma subtypes. OCTA is emerging as a complementary vascular biomarker; peripapillary vessel density shows the most consistent link to progression, with early evidence that vascular changes may precede detectable structural or functional decline. Deep learning models increasingly use raw or multimodal imaging rather than summary parameters; foundation and multimodal architectures (e.g., RETFound-based) show strong diagnostic performance and improved generalizability across demographics and disease severity. However, AI-based progression prediction remains less robust than cross-sectional diagnosis, especially under external validation. Portable/home-based OCT may extend monitoring beyond the clinic, though clinical utility remains investigational. The field is moving toward multimodal, longitudinal, AI-supported glaucoma assessment integrating structural, vascular, and functional biomarkers rather than interpreting them in isolation. Key priorities for translation include standardized acquisition and analysis across devices, large and diverse external validation cohorts, interpretable models, and evidence that AI and remote imaging improve clinically meaningful outcomes. These developments should make OCT increasingly central to earlier detection and individualized monitoring of glaucoma, but none currently replace established structural and functional assessment or clinical judgment.

desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] This chapter explores the transformative impact of artificial intelligence (AI)-augmented wearable technology in dynamic health monitoring across diagnosis, treatment, and rehabilitation. Innovations include real-time cardiovascular disease detection, AI-driven continuous glucose monitoring for diabetes, and neurological disorder tracking using flexible electroencephalograph (EEG) sensors. Therapeutic advances feature smart drug-delivery patches responsive to biomarkers, remote intervention systems, and surgical tools like augmented reality (AR) navigation. Rehabilitation breakthroughs encompass wearables for motor recovery, cardiopulmonary optimization, and neurorehabilitation using brain-computer interfaces. Future progress hinges on multifunctional hardware, federated learning for privacy, explainable AI, and standardized regulations.

Artificial intelligence in primary care: perceptions, implementation, and what it means for clinical practice.
desc: [Family practice] Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly integrated into primary care, yet its adoption is shaped by clinician and patient perceptions, workflow integration, and ethical and system-level considerations. The rapid evolution of generative AI introduces new opportunities and challenges that remain poorly understood. To map and synthesize the literature on AI in primary care, characterize clinician and patient perceptions, identify barriers and facilitators to implementation, and examine the implications of generative AI. We conducted a PRISMA-ScR scoping review of studies published from 2020 onward. Six databases were searched, supplemented by gray literature and hand-searching. Data were synthesized descriptively and thematically. Thirty-two studies were included. Family physicians reported benefits including improved workflow efficiency, documentation support, and clinical decision-making, alongside concerns regarding trust, accuracy, workflow integration, and medico-legal accountability. Patients generally supported AI when clinician oversight was maintained. Generative AI, particularly ambient documentation systems, improved workflow but introduced risks including hallucinated outputs, authorship ambiguity, and increased verification burden. Across studies, trust, workflow integration, and preservation of relational care consistently emerged as key determinants of successful AI adoption. AI has considerable potential to enhance primary care, but successful adoption depends less on technological capability than on strengthening trust, integrating into clinical workflows, and preserving relational care. As generative AI becomes embedded in practice, education, governance, and oversight will be essential to ensure safe, equitable, and patient-centered care.

Agentic AI and related systems in nursing and nursing-adjacent work: a scoping review of task allocation, decision authority, and accountability.
desc: [Frontiers in public health] Agentic artificial intelligence (AI) and related systems are being investigated for nursing and nursing-adjacent work, but inconsistent terminology and heterogeneous evaluations obscure their operational capabilities and clinical relevance. This review examined the relationship between reported agentic behavior, evaluation in nursing practice, retained decision authority, and evidence concerning patient benefit, workload, and accountability. We conducted a scoping review informed by JBI guidance and reported in accordance with PRISMA-ScR. We searched PubMed, Embase, CINAHL, Scopus, and Web of Science, supplemented by citation and linked-report searching. Among 28 reports, 13 satisfied all criteria, four were indeterminate, and 11 lacked at least one criterion. Only two qualifying reports evaluated live nurse-AI workflows. Nursing participation ranged from clinical work to education, co-design, output rating, and outcome assessment, and did not uniformly represent runtime control. Patient-facing clinical workflows retained professional decision authority; robotics evaluations involved neither nurses nor patients. Outcomes principally concerned technical performance, communication, usability, or component-specific efficiency. The evidence did not establish autonomous nursing practice, sustained patient benefit, or reduced complete-episode nursing workload. No empirical evaluation of accountability or redress following AI-related error was identified. Operational qualification, clinical benefit, and accountable use require separate evaluation. Future studies should assess the complete human-AI pathway, including verification, correction, escalation, patient outcomes, and responses to failure. Comparative designs should isolate agentic mechanisms from additional computation, information access, and workflow redesign. A proposed post hoc, unvalidated heuristic links allocated function, decision authority, assurance, and accountability/redress. Interpretation is limited by absent prospective registration, unquantified agreement before consensus, related reports, and the absence of formal risk-of-bias assessment. Agentic capability alone does not establish clinical readiness. Expanding AI-enabled functions requires evidence of meaningful benefit, effective human control, and accountability arrangements proportionate to the consequences of system actions.

Racial Disparities in Postpartum Morbidity and Mortality: A Systematic Review of Structural and Healthcare Systems Factors With AI/ML Applications.
source: PubMed · International journal of MCH and AIDS
desc: [International journal of MCH and AIDS] Racial disparities in maternal and postpartum health remain substantial in the United States. In 2024, the maternal mortality rate among non-Hispanic Black women was 44.8 deaths per 100,000 live births, compared with 14.2 among non-Hispanic White women. This systematic review synthesized contemporary evidence on racial disparities in postpartum morbidity and mortality, contributing structural and healthcare factors, emerging artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions intended to improve postpartum outcomes and equity. This systematic review was conducted in accordance with the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement. The evidence synthesis focused on U.S.-based primary empirical studies and authoritative government surveillance and analytic sources addressing maternal and postpartum outcomes, racial and ethnic disparities, structural and social determinants of health, healthcare access, artificial intelligence and machine-learning applications, and interventions relevant to postpartum health. We used systematic and scoping reviews for citation identification and contextual interpretation but did not count them as independent primary evidence. Because of substantial heterogeneity in study designs, populations, exposures, and outcomes, findings were synthesized narratively. The evidence demonstrated persistent racial and ethnic disparities across maternal mortality, severe maternal morbidity and postpartum hemorrhage, peripartum cardiomyopathy and hypertensive disorders, postpartum mental health, and access to postpartum care. Gut microbiome functional genomics and PBPK modeling: a systems framework for precision therapeutics.
desc: [Folia microbiologica] The gut microbiome is increasingly recognized as an important determinant of interindividual variability in the disposition and response to pharmaceuticals, nutraceuticals, and dietary bioactives. Conventional microbiome profiling based primarily on taxonomic composition provides limited mechanistic insight into these effects, whereas functional genomics and multi-omics approaches enable characterization of microbial genes, enzymes, pathways, and metabolites involved in xenobiotic biotransformation. This review examines the integration of gut microbiome functional genomics with physiologically based pharmacokinetic (PBPK) modeling as a systems framework for precision therapeutics. Particular emphasis is placed on translating microbial gene-enzyme-metabolite relationships and experimentally characterized biotransformation kinetics into quantitative PBPK parameters. Metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, metaproteomics, and metabolomics provide complementary information for resolving microbial metabolic potential and activity, while genome-scale and community metabolic models can identify candidate pathways for xenobiotic transformation and metabolite production. Microbiome-aware PBPK approaches may incorporate microbial biotransformation, metabolite formation, gastrointestinal transit, absorption, and temporal functional variability. Whether these additions improve exposure predictions requires evaluation against conventional PBPK models using independent pharmacokinetic datasets.Artificial intelligence and machine learning may further support functional feature identification and hybrid PBPK modeling, provided that predictions remain biologically interpretable and experimentally validated. Despite its potential, clinical translation is constrained by limited standardized kinetic data, microbiome variability, incomplete functional annotation, and insufficient prospective validation. Integrating validated microbial functional information with mechanistic PBPK modeling may ultimately provide a quantitative basis for microbiome-informed prediction of drug and nutraceutical exposure and advance individualized therapeutic strategies.

title: Insights into Channelopathies and Sport: The Genotype-Positive/Phenotype-Negative Athlete from Molecular Diagnosis to Management.
desc: [Sports medicine (Auckland, N.Z.)] Channelopathies, diseases with ion channel perturbations, are a major cause of sudden cardiac death in athletes. Advances in genetic testing have identified a growing population of athletes carrying (likely) pathogenic variants in cardiac ion channel genes who remain phenotypically silent. These genotype-positive/phenotype-negative (G+/P-) individuals present a distinct clinical challenge. Standard preparticipation screening, designed around phenotypic findings, provides little guidance for their management. A critical gap exists in providing prognostic guidance based on the involved gene, specific variants, and its molecular consequences. Beyond a critical review of existing literature, we provide a mechanistically anchored framework for variant-specific arrhythmic risk stratification across the major channelopathy genes. For each gene, we translate molecular pathophysiology into clinically actionable risk profiles and examine how exercise-specific triggers, including adrenergic surge, electrolyte shifts, and sympathovagal imbalance, interact with the underlying molecular substrate to modulate arrhythmic vulnerability. Standard diagnostic tools ranging from electro- and echocardiography, exercise stress testing, and pharmacological provocation to emerging modalities such as electroanatomic mapping and magnetocardiography are evaluated for their capacity to unmask subclinical disease and refine sports eligibility decisions. The case for an interdisciplinary sports-cardio-genetic board is made alongside a call for international collaborative registries, as existing evidence in G+/P- athletes is largely absent. The integration of artificial intelligence and telemonitoring into longitudinal athletic surveillance is discussed as a pragmatic strategy for early phenotype detection. Ultimately, guidance for the G+/P- athlete rests on a thorough understanding of the causative genetic variant and its pathophysiological consequences.

title: [AI-based analysis of orthopedic data : Fundamentals and practical examples].
desc: [Orthopadie (Heidelberg, Germany)] Artificial intelligence (AI) holds great promise for enhancing efficiency and alleviating workload within the healthcare system. Although AI-driven image analysis is already well established in clinical practice, its potential to extract meaningful insights from numerical orthopedic data remains largely underexploited. This article outlines the fundamentals and model development of AI, along with an overview of established learning methods. Using practical examples, the functionality and clinical utility of classification, regression, and clustering models are illustrated. AI-based analyses can uncover complex relationships within multifaceted patient data that, due to the large number of simultaneously considered parameters and their interactions, cannot be fully captured, even by experienced experts. Consequently, they serve as valuable decision-support tools, enabling more informed, data-driven, and efficient clinical decision-making. Combined with wearable sensor technology, AI further opens new avenues for remote, real-time telemedical monitoring and early detection of clinical changes. AI holds substantial potential to enhance clinical quality and reduce practitioner workload. However, it also raises important concerns regarding transparency, data privacy, and accountability. Consequently, AI should be regarded as a decision-support tool rather than a substitute for clinical expertise.

title: The current state of artificial intelligence and adolescent mental health: the promise and perils of a new frontier.
source: PubMed · Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care
desc: [Current problems in pediatric and adolescent health care] Adolescent mental health remains a topic of concern in the United States and worldwide. The COVID-19 pandemic accelerated the youth mental health crisis, which began nearly a decade earlier. The ongoing shortage of mental health professionals, including therapists and child and adolescent psychiatrists, means many adolescents who require mental health treatment do not receive it. The emergence of artificial intelligence (AI) technology has demonstrated promise in the field of adolescent mental health, including in screening, detection and risk prediction, intervention and treatment, clinical decision support and workflow augmentation, and in the training of future mental health professionals. However, the study of AI tools in the mental health space remains in its infancy, and most are not yet ready for routine use in clinical practice. Furthermore, the potential risks of AI and its use in adolescent mental health treatment are significant and must be addressed prior to widespread use. Health care professionals, adolescents, and their caregivers need to develop AI literacy to use the technology safely and responsibly. Additionally, AI governance and legal frameworks are necessary to ensure that AI technology use is safe, equitable and ethical for all users. At the present time, AI technology should serve a supportive and complementary role to human-delivered adolescent mental health care.

title: AI-assisted high-throughput screening of MOFs for formaldehyde capture.
desc: [Journal of hazardous materials] Formaldehyde (FA) is a hazardous indoor volatile organic compound that poses risks to human health, demanding efficient adsorbent materials. Functionalized Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) offer structural tunability; however, functionalization can alter the framework, increase heterogeneity, cause pore blockage, and increase cost. Identification of pristine MOFs for FA adsorption is crucial for understanding adsorption mechanisms, framework topology, chemical composition, and unfunctionalized structures. In this work, we present an AI-assisted high-throughput screening framework that combines Generative Artificial Intelligence (GAI)-based text mining, Grand Canonical Monte Carlo (GCMC) simulations, and Machine Learning (ML) to accelerate the discovery of MOFs for FA capture. Four MOF features were extracted using GAI text mining, and 1208 MOFs were selected from the CoRE MOF 2019 database. GCMC simulations evaluated FA uptake, while atomic, geometric, chemical, and thermodynamic descriptors were extracted for ML analyses. Seven regressors were developed to predict FA uptake based on these descriptors. An SVR-based denoising method was introduced during preprocessing to reduce simulation noise and improve predictions. The SVR model showed the best performance with an R² value of 0.94 and predicted FA uptake in 500 hMOFs. Validation of GAI responses, feature analyses, and experimental data also confirmed the reliability of this approach.

title: Patient-related aspects for health technology assessment of digital health technologies: a scoping review to inform the EDiHTA framework.
source: PubMed · International journal of technology assessment in health care
desc: [International journal of technology assessment in health care] To identify the topics and outcome measures used to evaluate patient-related aspects of digital health technologies (DHTs), and to propose a comprehensive framework to guide evidence requirements for their assessment in health technology assessments (HTA). A scoping review was conducted to identify the topics and outcome measures for the evaluation of patient-related aspects of DHTs. Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane CENTRAL, Web of Science, and CINAHL were searched. Extracted data included article identifiers, type of tool used for evaluation, topics, outcome measures, intended purpose of the DHT, and Artificial Intelligence capability according to the European Digital Health Technology Assessment (EDiHTA) taxonomy. Descriptive analyses were undertaken to summarize methods, topics, and outcome measures. A thematic analysis of measurement items was then conducted to address conceptual overlap. Finally, outcome measures were mapped to the Warwick Patient Experiences Framework (WaPEF). 336 articles were included in this review. Patient-related aspects were evaluated using qualitative methods (n = 164), non-validated tools (n = 127), and validated tools (n = 119). From the validated tools, twelve topics and 155 outcome measures were identified. After resolving conceptual overlaps, these were refined to nine topics and twenty-eight outcome measures. Most outcome measures mapped to WaPEF; however, two topics, caregiver burden and satisfaction, were not fully captured by WaPEF. This review proposes a framework for evaluating patient-related aspects in HTA of DHTs, comprising nine topics and twenty-eight outcome measures. By focusing on outcome measures, the framework improves conceptual clarity and supports a more systematic, and patient-centered approach to DHT evaluation.

title: Long-term tracking of individual pigs through re-identification.
desc: [Smart agricultural technology] Livestock production benefits from automated monitoring of animal health and welfare. However, continuous tracking of commercial pigs using Computer Vision (CV) is hindered by their uniform appearance, the need to avoid reliance on physical tags in commercial settings, and changes in appearance due to growth and dirt. This study addresses longitudinal tracking through an open-set Re-Identification (ReID) framework based on deep metric learning, designed to maintain the identities of visually uniform group-housed pigs without artificial or natural marks. A ResNet50 backbone was fine-tuned with a combined ArcFace and semi-hard triplet loss on a large-scale longitudinal dataset of visually uniform pigs. To mitigate embedding drift, a multi-anchor voting algorithm matched daily cluster centroids against a rolling bank of historical identity representations, while custom synthetic dirt augmentation prevented overfitting to transient dirt patterns. Three modalities were evaluated: Instance Segmentation (IS), Oriented Bounding Boxes (OBB) and Axis-Aligned Bounding Boxes (AABB). During an 18-day open-set evaluation, the multi-anchor framework reached a mean tracking accuracy of 88.0% with IS images, outperforming a sequential day-to-day baseline (54.6%). OBB performance was comparable to IS at lower computational cost, whereas AABB degraded to 51.4%, attributed to background noise. Without synthetic dirt augmentation, tracking fell to 56.5% for IS images. An adapted GradCAM showed consistent attention to body regions such as the head, shoulder and rear, suggesting that identification may rely on stable anatomical traits rather than transient artefacts. These findings indicate that ReID of visually uniform pigs is feasible without physical tags, a step toward non-invasive, continuous welfare monitoring in precision livestock farming.

title: Modeling brake wear particle emissions under diverse driving conditions: A data-driven time-series approach.
desc: [Journal of hazardous materials] With the forthcoming Euro 7 regulation, the representativeness of brake particle emissions measured under the WLTP-Brake cycle has received increasing attention. In this study, two pad materials from different vehicles were tested on a brake dynamometer under multiple driving conditions. Although PM10 emissions under the WLTP-Brake cycle complied with the regulatory limit, exceedances occurred under other conditions. Variations in PN emissions among cycles reflected the cumulative effects of preceding brake events, indicating strong temporal dependence. Machine-learning models were therefore developed to predict PN emissions and identify influential brake features. Under time-series inputs, the Transformer achieved the best predictive performance, with an R2 of 0.85 ± 0.03, while XGBoost also showed acceptable accuracy. SHAP analysis showed that high-emission tests were mainly associated with positive contributions from temperature and brake power, whereas low-emission tests were characterized by negative contributions from features such as vehicle speed. Speed was positively related to PN emissions, and brake power amplified its influence. Overall, the proposed approach enables brake particle emissions to be evaluated under diverse driving conditions and may support future brake-emission assessment and regulation.

title: Chatbots and Social Media-Embedded AI Assistants Provide Inconsistent Information on the Use of Unregulated Peptides Marketed for Musculoskeletal Recovery.
source: PubMed · HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery
desc: [HSS journal : the musculoskeletal journal of Hospital for Special Surgery] Unregulated peptides like BPC-157 are heavily marketed for musculoskeletal recovery despite the lack of U.S. Food and Drug Administration approval and minimal evidence from human trials. With peptide content widely promoted on social media, patients increasingly consult artificial intelligence (AI) tools to evaluate claims regarding the efficacy of these products. We sought to compare the accuracy, completeness, and readability of AI-generated information on unregulated peptides for musculoskeletal recovery across dedicated AI tools and social-media-embedded assistants. We performed a cross-sectional content analysis study of AI outputs in response to 4 standardized questions about unapproved peptide use. Seven dedicated AI tools (ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, OpenEvidence, Elicit, Undermind, and Consensus.ai) and 4 social-media assistants (Instagram, Facebook, TikTok, and X) were queried in May 2026. Readability was assessed using a composite of 4 grade-level formulas. Two evidence-anchored questions were scored by 3 blinded reviewers (2 orthopedic surgeons and 1 immunopathologist) using the validated Quality Assessment of Medical Artificial Intelligence (QAMAI) instrument (6-30) for the 7 dedicated AI tools but not for the 4 social media assistants. Mean QAMAI score across the dedicated tools was 21.6/30 (good), ranging from 17.8 (Undermind, fair) to 25.3 (Claude, very good). Among dedicated tools, pooled QAMAI domain scores were highest for accuracy (4.0/5) and lowest for completeness (3.3/5). Among social-media assistants, X and Facebook were accurate, TikTok was mixed, and Instagram (Meta AI) spread misinformation, claiming BPC-157 accelerates recovery and endorsing post-surgical use. All 11 tools produced outputs at the college level (mean grade: 13.9), above the sixth-to-eighth-grade target for patient materials, with no correlation between quality and readability. Our analysis suggests that AI tools cannot substitute for clinical counseling on unregulated peptides. The accuracy subscore was generally strong, but completeness and readability remained poor. Medical societies should partner with AI developers to standardize evidence-anchored responses and prevent patient harm. Level IV: observational content analysis study.

title: LesionAgent: Training-Free Agentic Tumor Tracking and Response Assessment in Longitudinal CT
desc: Every few months, a cancer patient's CT scans decide whether treatment continues. 3D foundation models can now detect, segment, register and track lesions, yet none of them reads the scans as a radiologist does. A radiologist decides which findings are lesions, which are the same lesion months later and whether a new spot means progression, and checks each decision against the extensive rules of a clinical guideline. We introduce LesionAgent, an LLM agent that performs this read end to end without task-specific training. It operates frozen 3D models as tools, acts in 3D through coordinate-labelled views, remembers every lesion across visits in a registry, verifies every model output it relies on, and leaves every number to a deterministic guideline engine. On four public longitudinal CT datasets, LesionAgent tracks more lesions and measures them more accurately than every automatic basel

title: MicroBioAgent: an AI agent for automated microbiome analysis
desc: Microbiome data analysis demands customized workflows tailored to specific biological questions, sequencing modalities, and data properties. However, constructing and executing these workflows requires navigating heterogeneous software dependencies, reference databases, and multi-step parameter tuning. Here, we present MicroBioAgent, an autonomous, domain-specific agent framework that translates high-level biological queries into executable, study-specific pipelines across 16S rRNA amplicon, reference-based shotgun, and de novo assembly-based metagenomics. Rather than relying on static pipeline templates, MicroBioAgent employs a closed-loop execution architecture: it dynamically selects and runs bioinformatics tools within user-controlled environments while iteratively inspecting intermediate outputs to adapt downstream analytical decisions. Furthermore, to address the long-running nature of metagenomic computation, we introduce an asynchronous background task-management mechanism that reduces LLM token consumption by over 50% while enabling real-time plan adjustment and automated workflow resumption. We systematically evaluated MicroBioAgent across three benchmarks of increasing complexity: (1) paired amplicon and shotgun profiling of tomato rhizosphere microbiomes, (2) taxonomic and functional profiling coupled with machine-learning classification in a colorectal cancer cohort, and (3) de novo metagenomic assembly, metagenome-assembled genome (MAG) binning, and metabolic pathway reconstruction in a polyethylene degradation study. Across all benchmarks, MicroBioAgent faithfully recapitulated the primary biological findings of the original studies, exhibiting high analytical concordance despite expected tool- and database-dependent variations. In systematic robustness evaluations across 27 independent runs spanning three backbone large language models and three prompt-complexity tiers, MicroBioAgent achieved a 98.8% task completion rate and yielded highly reproducible diversity and differential-abundance estimates. MicroBioAgent establishes a scalable, adaptive paradigm for end-to-end computational microbiome research.

source: PubMed · Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)
desc: [Methods in molecular biology (Clifton, N.J.)] Multi-omics integration amalgamates genomic, transcriptomic, epigenomic, and proteomic layers to provide a systems-level portrait of multifaceted diseases such as cancer. However, its practical application faces constraints posed by challenges including elevated dimensionality, diverse data types, and prevalent missing values. This review delivers a structured summary of recent advances in machine-learning-driven integration of multi-omics datasets, with a specific emphasis on the potential of this field for translational cancer research. First, we discuss the importance of multi-omics integration. Next, we provide an overview of key machine learning methodologies, including high-dimensional variable selection techniques (e.g., knockoff filters for controlling the false discovery rate), deep learning models (for survival prediction and classification), and generative models (e.g., diffusion models and variational autoencoders for data augmentation and missing data imputation). These approaches demonstrate high accuracy in cancer subtype classification, biomarker discovery, prognosis evaluation, and personalized therapy. For example, they achieve over 85% accuracy in triple-negative breast cancer subtype analysis. We also cover the contributions of single-cell multi-omics technologies (e.g., SHARE-seq and SNARE-seq) and emerging databases (e.g., scImmOmics and scCancerExplorer) to enhancing data resolution. While challenges remain in terms of interpretability and computational efficiency, integrating explainable AI and multimodal learning shows promise in accelerating clinical translation. This review seeks to equip researchers with a systematic methodological roadmap and demonstrate its practical utility in precision medicine via exemplar case studies.

title: Scalable Evaluation of Medical AI using Evidence-based Practice Recommendations
desc: Rigorously evaluating medical artificial intelligence (AI) requires testing open-ended clinical management across diverse presentations and stages of care. However, existing benchmarks rely on manual expert authoring, limiting coverage across conditions, conditional care pathways, and evolving guidelines. We develop an automated pipeline that extracts and verifies structured clinical criteria and branching decision trees from practice recommendations to generate scenarios spanning the care continuum, including nuanced presentations and practice variations across regions and guideline editions. title: An open long non-coding RNA foundation model for generalizable prediction
desc: Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) play essential roles in transcriptional regulation and chromatin organization, yet predicting their functional properties from sequence remains challenging because informative signals span both local motifs and long-range base pairing across kilobase-scale transcripts. Current RNA foundation models are restricted to short sequences and existing lncRNA prediction models narrowly focus on isolated tasks, leaving a dedicated foundation model notably absent. Here we present LncRFM, a dedicated lncRNA foundation model, supported by the LncCorpus pretraining data and the LncBench evaluation suite, which stand for a systematic framework to decode lncRNAs. For foundation model pretraining, we develop a hybrid bidirectional state-space encoder trained with a structure-guided masking strategy to effectively capture both local sequence patterns and long-range contexts. For pretraining data, we contribute over 9.6 million lncRNA sequences to assemble LncCorpus, a pretraining corpus of 24.7 million sequences. For benchmarking evaluation, we construct a comprehensive benchmark, LncBench, comprising 15 datasets and totaling over 1,010,000 sequences across 10 prediction tasks: six core lncRNA functional and annotation tasks and four structural and regulatory RNA assay tasks. Evaluated against seven RNA foundation models under a unified frozen-encoder protocol, our LncRFM achieves the state-of-the-art primary-metric scores on 11 of the 13 datasets that allow downstream adaptation. On two external generalization benchmarks evaluated without further adaptation, LncRFM matches the best structure-specialized baseline in F1 (0.141) and achieves the highest AUROC (0.962) on lncRNA contact prediction, while maintaining competitive cross-species coding-potential transfer (F1 of 0.374) under severe multi-kingdom domain shift. To benefit the scientific community, we make all datasets, source code, and pretrained models publicly available.

Machine learning and deep learning for predicting acute exacerbation in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: a systematic review.
desc: [Systematic reviews] Acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) imposes a substantial burden on patients and healthcare systems. Although traditional risk assessment tools exist, machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) may offer improved prediction. This systematic review aims to evaluate the performance of ML and DL algorithms for predicting AECOPD risk. This review was conducted in accordance with the PRISMA guidelines. PubMed, Embase, Cochrane Library and Web of Science were systematically searched from 1 January 2021 to 6 May 2026. Studies that developed or validated ML and DL models for predicting AECOPD risk were included. Methodological quality, risk of bias and applicability were assessed using the PROBAST + AI, and reporting quality was assessed using the TRIPOD + AI. Because of substantial heterogeneity, we synthesised model performance descriptively. Thirteen studies were included, of which only two performed external validation. Overall, reported AUC values ranged widely from 0.661 to 0.9721. By outcome type, AUC values for AECOPD risk prediction ranged from 0.668 to 0.9721, whereas those for AECOPD‑related hospitalisation ranged from 0.661 to 0.885. Similarly, by prediction windows, short‑term prediction achieved AUCs of 0.668‑0.972, compared with 0.661‑0.884 for long‑term prediction. However, PROBAST + AI revealed high methodological quality concerns and risk of bias in all 13 studies, and TRIPOD + AI showed suboptimal reporting transparency with an overall completeness rate of 54.3%. Limited evidence indicates that models for any AECOPD may outperform those for hospitalisation, and that models with shorter prediction windows may show higher AUCs, although this association could be confounded by small sample sizes and potential patient-level leakage. These findings provide valuable direction for future model development and validation, although the current evidence base is constrained by methodological quality concerns, risk of bias and suboptimal reporting transparency. title: Evidence sufficiency assessment enables cost-effective review allocation in on-premise clinical AI agents
desc: On-premise clinical AI agents must auto-accept high-confidence diagnoses, deferring others to clinician review, yet token probabilities and self-reported confidence miss errors, while more reliable five-run consistency incurs fivefold compute. We propose training-free decision-point evidence sufficiency assessment and a three-tier sequential triage protocol. Masking reasoning and diagnosis, the same 4B model scores sufficiency from objective evidence via prior-debiased probabilities over five ordered levels. Calibration freezes a nominal top-50% threshold, selecting single-run, five-run consistency, or full-deferral tiers by whether the one-sided 95% Wilson lower confidence bound of pass rate among accepted cases meets the 95% clinical target line. Across 1,605 MIRA-v2, CDM, VivaBench, and in-hospital liver malignancy primary cohort cases, MIRA-v2 single-run top-50% pass rate reached 98.

title: A Scoping Review on Large Language Model Clinical Decision Support in Acute and Critical Care.
desc: [Journal of medical systems] Decision-making in acute and critical care relies on interpretation of heterogeneous information sources under substantial time pressure. Large language models (LLMs) have been proposed as clinical decision support systems (CDSS) to aid in triage, diagnosis generation, and treatment planning. This scoping review maps the current landscape of LLM-based CDSS in acute and critical care and assesses their readiness for clinical implementation. A PRISMA-ScR-guided search of four databases (January 2026) yielded 62 studies, including 15 medical domain-adapted LLMs. Technology Readiness Levels were assigned across all 62 studies; none has progressed to clinical deployment. Within the medical LLM subgroup, medical LLMs generally outperformed their foundation model counterparts, although the evidence was heterogeneous. An exploratory PROBAST + AI-informed appraisal identified recurring methodological concerns, and thematic synthesis of implementation determinants identified regulatory constraints, workflow integration, and insufficient understanding of human-AI interaction as key barriers. This review highlights priorities for prospective validation using real-world institutional data.

title: Leakage-Free Is Not Confounder-Free: What a Patient-Level Split Cannot Certify About a Medical Imaging Benchmark
desc: Patient-level splitting is the standard safeguard against subject leakage in medical imaging evaluation, but it cannot remove a confounder that every fold inherits: an acquisition variable aligned with the diagnosis across the whole cohort. We present a five-question audit of a candidate confounder: how well it predicts the diagnosis, whether it can be decoded from the images, whether diagnostic scores depend on it, whether the image adds predictive value beyond it and how much discrimination survives once it is controlled. We apply it to DMR-IR, the public dataset on which most machine-learning results in breast thermography rest. On 236 patients under a strict patient-disjoint protocol, the acquisition date alone predicts malignancy at AUROC 0.980, above the best of nine imaging arms (0.949), because benign and malignant patients were recruited in different years. title: AI-Driven Augmented Reality for Obstructive Sleep Apnea: An Emerging Frontier in Diagnosis, Treatment, and Self-Management.
source: PubMed · Nature and science of sleep
desc: [Nature and science of sleep] Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) remains one of the most prevalent yet underdiagnosed chronic disorders worldwide, with persistent challenges in timely diagnosis and long-term adherence to continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy. Artificial intelligence (AI) and augmented reality (AR) have emerged as promising digital health technologies that address complementary aspects of OSA management. AI has demonstrated strong diagnostic performance under controlled conditions in automated OSA detection, severity classification, and physiological signal analysis, whereas AR is being tested as a way to improve CPAP mask fitting, patient education, and treatment engagement. However, the integration of these technologies has received little attention in either the scientific literature or clinical practice. This commentary highlights the emerging convergence of AI and AR as a novel paradigm for OSA diagnosis, treatment initiation, and self-management. Current evidence indicates that AI-driven AR applications are beginning to appear at the commercial level, yet robust OSA-specific clinical evidence remains limited. Potential applications include AR-guided home diagnostic setup, AI-assisted CPAP mask fitting and desensitization, and personalized AR-based coaching to support long-term treatment adherence. We also discuss key barriers to implementation, including the limited evidence base, algorithmic bias from training data that underrepresent some populations, the privacy of sleep and facial data, the digital divide that affects older and low-income patients, regulatory pathways, and uncertainties regarding clinical integration. Finally, we propose a research agenda, guided by implementation science frameworks, focused on feasibility, usability, patient acceptability, and comparative effectiveness against existing educational and telemedicine approaches, to determine whether AI-driven AR represents a meaningful advance in OSA care. Establishing this evidence base will be essential for translating this emerging technological convergence into routine clinical practice.

title: Observed, Curated, Reused: Observation Bias in Clinical AI Evaluation
desc: Clinical AI evaluations are vulnerable to observation bias embedded in routine medical documentation, which captures only what clinicians notice, test, and record rather than a complete clinical picture. As this evidence travels into publications and reference knowledge graphs, crucial distinctions disappear: unexamined symptoms blur with confirmed negatives, and chronological disease progression is lost. Surviving evidence can also enter both the benchmark query and the reference knowledge base, creating a self-referential loop where a patient is evaluated against clues derived from their own published case report. title: From Gene Sets to Brain Function: A Physiology-Informed Framework for Multi-Omics Integration in Precision Neurophysiology.
source: PubMed · Chronic diseases and translational medicine
desc: [Chronic diseases and translational medicine] Public omics repositories and multi-omics technologies have substantially expanded the molecular characterization of chronic human diseases by enabling large-scale analyses across diverse biological and clinical contexts. However, in neurological disorders, translating omics-derived associations into mechanistic insight and clinical relevance remains challenging due to the dynamic and multiscale nature of brain function. Gene set-based analytical approaches effectively identify enriched molecular patterns, but are limited in capturing temporal dynamics, network-level interactions, and physiological state dependence that define neural systems. This conceptual methodological review synthesizes foundational infrastructure papers, methodological evaluations, and translational neuroscience literature to critically examine the application of public omics resources in human neurophysiology, focusing on the interpretive gap between molecular-level associations and functional brain processes. We examine major public omics infrastructures, widely used gene set analysis frameworks, the principal strategies for multi-omics integration, and the challenge of batch effects in public data reuse, highlighting both their analytical strengths and structural limitations. Core neurophysiological principles, including synaptic transmission, network dynamics, plasticity, and homeostatic regulation, are discussed to clarify why direct inference from static molecular profiles to brain function is inherently constrained. Clinical illustrations from epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and migraine demonstrate how chronic neurological disorders emerge from context-dependent neural dynamics that are not readily reducible to gene set-level summaries. Finally, we outline future directions for integrating artificial intelligence with public omics resources, emphasizing physiology-informed modeling, explainable AI, and ethical considerations to support more interpretable and translational precision health strategies in chronic neurological disease.

title: Neurodegenerative Differential Diagnosis with Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning
desc: Accurate differential diagnosis of neurodegenerative disorders remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and heterogeneous, often incomplete multimodal observations. Existing multimodal models can integrate imaging and clinical measurements but often overlook disease-specific evidence patterns and pairwise relations among competing diagnoses. We therefore propose Knowledge-enhanced Structural Reasoning (KnowSR), which aligns multimodal patient representations with a literature-grounded knowledge bank of disease prototypes, signed evidence directions, and pairwise diagnostic relations. title: Deep Learning for Generating Computational PIN-4 Immunohistochemistry Staining from Prostate Biopsy H&E Images.
source: PubMed · Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications
desc: [Proceedings of the ... International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications. International Conference on Machine Learning and Applications] Immunohistochemistry (IHC) staining is frequently used to resolve diagnostically ambiguous prostate cancer biopsy findings on hematoxylin and eosin (H&E)-stained tissue. However, PIN-4 IHC is typically performed on adjacent tissue sections, limiting direct spatial comparison between the H&E morphology that indicated the need for IHC and the corresponding immunophenotypic signal. A paired, registered H&E/PIN-4 dataset was constructed from routine clinical prostate biopsy whole-slide images (WSIs), and a conditional generative adversarial network (cGAN) was trained to synthesize PIN-4 staining patterns directly from native H&E image patches. The final dataset comprised 172 paired WSIs from 93 patients and 27,298 registered 1024 × 1024 patch pairs, spanning adenocarcinoma-positive and benign cases with representation across age, race, and ethnicity groups. The model was evaluated on an independent held-out test set of 1,814 patch pairs from 17 WSIs, achieving a mean peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) of 21.88 dB, structural similarity index measure (SSIM) of 0.667, Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC) of 0.684, and learned perceptual image patch similarity (LPIPS) of 0.417. Qualitative review by a board-certified pathologist demonstrated that generated images captured diagnostically relevant PIN-4 staining patterns, including AMACR/racemase expression and basal-cell-associated staining, while preserving spatial correspondence with the source H&E morphology. Synthesis quality varied across morphologically complex regions, including high-grade carcinoma and intraductal carcinoma. These results support the feasibility of supervised computational PIN-4 staining from routinely acquired brightfield H&E prostate biopsy images. The approach enables direct interpretation of predicted PIN-4 marker patterns in the context of the source prostate H&E architecture, addressing a current spatial limitation of conventional adjacent-section IHC.

title: BioELX: Context-Aware Cross-lingual Biomedical Entity Linking without Task-Specific Supervision
desc: Cross-lingual biomedical entity linking (BEL) maps mentions in any language to unique identifiers in a biomedical knowledge base, supporting clinical and biomedical NLP applications. We identify two issues affecting current systems. First, the UMLS (Bodenreider,2004) aliases used to train cross-lingual BEL retrievers are heavily skewed toward English, so retrievers generalize poorly to non-English mentions. Second, although context is often necessary for disambiguation, naively injecting context into retrievers trained only to align aliases severely degrades retrieval. We propose BioELX, a retrieve-rerank framework that addresses both issues. For retrieval, we continue training SapBERT_multi (Liu et al., 2021b) using Wikidata-derived cross-lingual alias supervision, forming shared concept neighborhoods across languages. title: Tumor-draining lymph nodes as candidate sources of immunotherapy biomarkers in breast cancer: a multi-omics and artificial intelligence roadmap.
desc: [Biomarker research] Although immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) have transformed breast cancer treatment, predicting durable clinical benefit remains challenging. Current biomarkers, primarily derived from tumor tissue or peripheral blood, do not directly capture the adaptive immune response at its site of initiation. Tumor-draining lymph nodes (TDLNs) are not passive conduits for metastasis but dynamic immunological hubs where anti-tumor T cell priming and immune evasion converge. In this review, we critically examine the nascent intersection of TDLN immunobiology, high-resolution multi-omics, and artificial intelligence (AI) to evaluate TDLN-derived features as candidate next-generation biomarkers for immunotherapy. We synthesize the complex cellular and molecular architecture of the breast cancer TDLN, including T cell exhaustion, B cell-mediated immunity, and stromal crosstalk, before evaluating the state-of-the-art single-cell and spatial technologies capable of decoding this microenvironment. We assess the application of AI and foundation models in this domain, identifying a major methodological gap: while AI frameworks are increasingly mature for primary tumors, their application to TDLNs remains unvalidated and limited by a severe scarcity of annotated multi-omics datasets. Furthermore, we address pivotal translational considerations, including the immunological implications of axillary surgery in the ICI era. We emphasize that no TDLN-derived biomarker has yet undergone prospective validation as a predictive biomarker for immunotherapy in breast cancer, and that retrospective analyses of trial specimens must account for the timing of tissue acquisition relative to systemic therapy. Finally, we chart immediate research priorities, including establishing TDLN reference atlases and developing clinically feasible specimen collection pathways for biomarker validation. This review provides a conceptual framework and translational roadmap to assess whether TDLN-derived features can complement existing tumor-centric metrics in guiding immunotherapy decisions.

title: SecretAgent: A Multi-Agent Framework for Privacy Protection against Vision Language Models
desc: Vision-language models (VLMs) can infer private information from shared images, including locations, personally identifiable information (PII), and personal attributes such as age and sex, even from medical images. Adversarial perturbations can protect such information against black-box VLMs, but existing methods overlook image quality and introduce visible artifacts into the images they protect. We present SecretAgent, the first general multi-agent framework that protects image privacy against VLMs while preserving visual fidelity. LLM agents iteratively locate the visual evidence that reveals private information and adapt an invisible perturbation to the target VLM's answers and to an appearance reviewer agent, which rejects any candidate with visible artifacts. title: Integrative Multi-Omics in Glaucoma: Defining Mechanistic Axes and Enabling Precision Management.
desc: [Investigative ophthalmology & visual science] Glaucoma is increasingly recognized not as a uniform pressure-defined optic neuropathy, but rather as a heterogeneous neurodegenerative disorder driven by interacting genetic, metabolic, mechanical, vascular, inflammatory, and environmental factors. Although genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics, and metabolomics have each yielded important insights, no single omics layer can fully capture the multilevel architecture underlying differences in disease susceptibility, progression, and treatment response. Multi-omics therefore offers a more integrated framework for linking inherited risk, gene regulation, cellular states, protein activity, metabolic vulnerability, and imaging phenotypes to clinically relevant outcomes. This review summarizes recent advances in multi-omics research in glaucoma, spanning genomics, epigenomics and transcriptomics, proteomics, metabolomics and lipidomics, microbiome studies, and emerging approaches such as spatial omics, single-cell multi-omics, radiomics, and exposomics. We further discuss how cross-layer integration, network analysis, Mendelian randomization, imaging genomics, and multimodal artificial intelligence are helping to define convergent pathogenic pathways and clinically relevant molecular subtypes. Particular attention is given to four major pathological axes: extracellular matrix-mechanical stress, mitochondrial-metabolic dysfunction, immune-microbiome dysregulation, and exposure-vascular burden. Despite ongoing challenges in standardization, cohort size, validation, and interpretability, multi-omics is shifting glaucoma research toward mechanism-based stratification and deployable precision care.

title: Ruby: State-of-the-Art Potency Prediction across Discovery Regimes Using Learned Structural Representations
desc: Small-molecule drug discovery proceeds through repeated design-make-test-analyze cycles. The goal is often to maximize potency while keeping other properties within the ranges required for a viable therapeutic candidate. Compound prioritization places different demands on computational methods as drug discovery progresses from hit identification through hit-to-lead and lead optimization, with changing computational budgets and increasing amounts of on-target experimental data. We introduce Ruby, a Robust Universal Binding affinitY predictor that uses intermediate representations from the structural foundation model Pearl without requiring an explicit binding pose for every compound. Ruby is trained on proprietary data plus GenesisPotency-2026, an audited public-source potency training dataset released for academic and commercial use under a CC BY-SA 4.0 license with row-level provenance

title: AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses: a concept analysis.
desc: [BMC nursing] To clarify the concept of AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses and to provide a conceptual foundation for nursing education, clinical practice, and responsible AI governance. Rodgers' evolutionary concept analysis. Guided by Rodgers' evolutionary method, the literature was analyzed to determine how AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses has been used and conceptualized. Defining attributes, antecedents, consequences, and related concepts were extracted, compared, and synthesized. A systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, PubMed, Embase, and CINAHL. Search terms focused on nurses, nursing students, health workers, artificial intelligence literacy, algorithmic literacy, AI competence, AI readiness, and generative AI literacy. Articles published between January 2020 and June 2026 were screened. Twenty-eight articles were included in the final concept analysis. Four defining attributes were identified: conceptual understanding of AI-mediated nursing contexts; critical interpretation and risk recognition of algorithmic outputs; clinical integration and human oversight of AI recommendations; and ethical governance awareness grounded in professional accountability. Antecedents included AI education and training, digital or informatics foundations, prior AI exposure, individual readiness, organizational support, faculty preparedness, and governance environments. Consequences included improved learning outcomes, critical thinking, AI adoption and readiness, patient safety awareness, human-AI collaboration, and professional innovation. Related concepts included AI literacy, algorithmic literacy, digital literacy, nursing informatics competence, AI readiness, AI competence, and AI self-efficacy. Based on this synthesis, both a brief definition and a full conceptual definition of AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses were proposed. AI and algorithmic literacy among nurses is a multidimensional concept that extends beyond technical knowledge or willingness to use AI. It reflects nurses' ability to understand, interpret, supervise, and responsibly integrate AI outputs into nursing judgment while maintaining patient safety and professional accountability. Clarifying this concept can support the development of nursing AI education, competency frameworks, measurement tools, clinical training, and governance strategies. title: Learning 3D MRI Representations with Generative Adversarial Networks
desc: Learning representations of visual images is a challenging task. It requires extracting abstract patterns from high-dimensional data without explicit supervision. This becomes pronounced with 3D MR imaging due to sparse features, higher dimensional inputs, and smaller datasets. Many state-of-the-art representation learning algorithms successfully rely on transformers and diffusion-based architectures. However, these methods struggle with smaller datasets. In effect, solution methods relax the problem by slicing 3D volumes and solving the problem for 2D medical imaging, resulting in a loss of spatial 3D information. We present R2RG, a representation learning method based on Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs), with Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) honing the reconstruction task. title: Large Language Model-Powered AI-Assisted Simulated Patient for Nursing Education: Quasi-Experimental Study.
desc: [JMIR nursing] Large language model (LLM)-powered virtual patient systems are gaining popularity in nursing education but also face persistent challenges, such as hallucinations and role inconsistency. This paper reports the model architecture design, technical considerations, implementation challenges, and evaluation of an LLM-powered AI-assisted simulated-patient system integrated into a nursing triage simulation game. The system integrated a Unity-based game client, with GPT-4o hosted through Microsoft AI Foundry to support real-time simulated-patient dialogue in Traditional Chinese using Cantonese syntax. This developmental study comprised exploratory model selection, formative student feedback-informed enhancement from Version 1 to Version 2, development-stage script-fidelity evaluation, and evaluation of system usability and the Net Promoter Score in 2 tutorial cohorts of nursing students. Key technical contributions include a layered hallucination mitigation architecture that combines grounded prompt inclusion, few-shot conversational exemplars, negative role constraints, and calibrated model parameters. The implementation process also addresses stateless API memory management, cloud-based safety filter calibration for domain-specific clinical prompts, and prompt engineering strategies to prevent role drift and hidden scenario information leakage. GPT-4o was selected as the production model through exploratory development testing that considered script consistency, Cantonese-language suitability, response latency, technical reliability, deployment feasibility, cost considerations, and Unity integration compatibility; 45 of 50 (90%) assessed GPT-4o responses were rated fully script-consistent. This study demonstrates the development and real-world tutorial deployment of a Cantonese-language, LLM-powered simulated-patient system for nursing triage education. Integrating formative student feedback with structured technical debugging enabled iterative refinement of dialogue fidelity, role consistency, protected-information handling, and game interaction functions. The resulting Version 2 system provides a practical, contextually tailored approach to supporting scalable simulated-patient dialogue in nursing education.

title: DermKG: A Concept-Centric Knowledge Graph for Interpretable Skin Disease Diagnosis from Dermatological Morphology
desc: Dermatologists describe lesions with a standardized morphological lexicon, which makes concept-based models attractive for interpretable skin disease diagnosis. How much diagnostic information these concepts actually carry, however, is rarely quantified. desc: [Clinical genitourinary cancer] Agreement of large language models with multidisciplinary tumor board (MDT) decisions in metastatic hormone-sensitive prostate cancer is unknown. First-line MDT recommendations (2020-2023) were compared with those of GPT-4o configured with European Association of Urology guidelines and institutional procedures. Recommendations for androgen deprivation therapy (ADT), systemic intensification, and radiotherapy were classified as not recommended, optional, or recommended, and summarized as a normalized consensus score; agreement was assessed with Cohen's kappa (κ). Scoring weights were tested in sensitivity analyses; non-consensus cases were reviewed post hoc by 2 urologists. Full consensus occurred in 14.1%, partial consensus in 50.0%, and no consensus in 35.9%; full consensus did not exceed 37% under any alternative scoring scheme. Binary agreement was 88.5% for ADT (κ -0.05, prevalence effect), 56.4% for radiotherapy (κ 0.05), and 71.8% for systemic intensification (κ 0.25). GPT-4o recommended radiotherapy definitively in 11.5% (MDT 44.9%) and as optional in 64.1%, but never designated systemic intensification as optional. Reviewers attributed 19 of 28 non-consensus cases to information not available to the model. Agreement with documented MDT decisions was low and mainly reflected recommendation strength, particularly for radiotherapy. title: Embodied-Harness: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement for Robotic Manipulation
desc: Vision-language model (VLM)-based agents offer a promising approach to robotic manipulation, yet remain limited by inadequate memory organization, uncertain failure attribution, and limited reuse of execution experience. We propose Embodied-Harness, a dual-agent framework that improves manipulation by refining the execution harness without updating model parameters. The Actor interacts with the environment through a robot-control interface, while the Reflector converts execution evidence into reusable operational guidance. Hierarchical Memory Architecture maintains short-term execution context and long-term experiential knowledge to support execution and reflection. Evidence-based Experience Reflection grounds failure diagnosis in observed interactions, while Recursive Harness Self-Improvement refines operational guidance across successive attempts. title: Plant autoinhibited Ca2+-ATPases: shaping calcium signals for growth, stress adaptation, and crop improvement.
desc: [Frontiers in plant science] P-type ATPases are conserved ATP-driven ion transporters that maintain cellular ion homeostasis. Plant P-type IIB Ca2+-ATPases, known as autoinhibited Ca2+-ATPases (ACAs), are key regulators of Ca2+ signaling networks. This review summarizes the structural features, Ca2+/calmodulin-dependent regulation, evolutionary diversification, and biological functions of plant ACAs. By contributing to cytosolic Ca2+ clearance and the restoration of basal Ca2+ levels, ACAs may modulate stimulus-specific Ca2+ dynamics and participate in diverse physiological processes, including plant growth, development, stomatal movement, immunity, and abiotic stress adaptation. Comparative analyses across plant species highlight functional specialization of ACA isoforms and their potential value for crop improvement. We further discuss current challenges in ACA functional characterization, particularly the complexity of Ca2+ signaling networks and the limited understanding of ACA-associated genetic variation. Emerging approaches integrating multi-omics, artificial intelligence, and precision genome editing provide new opportunities for identifying and designing ACA alleles for climate-resilient crop breeding.

title: A Benchmark Protocol and Fairness Analysis Towards Open-Set EEG Seizure Type Classification
desc: Automated EEG seizure type classification systems are typically trained and evaluated under the closed-set assumption, where all seizure types encountered at deployment are seen during training. In clinical practice, this assumption fails: patients present with rare or atypical seizure types that fall outside the training label space, and a system that forces a wrong label is worse than one that abstains. We introduce the first open-set recognition protocol for EEG seizure type classification on the Temple University Hospital Seizure Corpus (TUSZ v2.0.3), defining known and unknown classes using the clinical taxonomy itself: seizure types with sufficient subject representation (at least 12 subjects) form the known set, and rare types form the unknown set. title: MorphoHELM: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating Representations for Microscopy-Based Morphology Assays
desc: Microscopy images contain rich information about how cells respond to perturbations, making them essential to applications like drug screening. To quantify images, researchers often use representation extraction methods, and recent years have seen a proliferation of deep learning methods. While measuring the quality of these representations is essential, evaluation remains fragmented, with each proposed model evaluated on different tasks and datasets, using custom pipelines and metrics, making it difficult to fairly compare models. Here, we introduce MorphoHELM, a comprehensive open benchmark for evaluating feature extraction methods for Cell Painting, the most widely-used morphological profiling assay. title: PathOPEN: A pathologist-curated histopathology dataset for visual question answering
desc: PathOPEN is a histopathology dataset for visual question answering. Two clinical pathologists selected 157 cases with 229 available original images and wrote open-ended, five-option multiple-choice and close-ended (yes/no) questions. They supplied both a correct and a wrong answer for 201 of the 309 open-ended questions. Each case records the organ, pathology category and regional anatomy, and each image records its magnification. The dataset includes 6,870 augmented images and four manifests that select subsets to improve balance by individual metadata field. Five additional pathologists and two vision-language model judges rated items with scoring rubrics, and six models answered questions zero-shot across the three formats. The metadata support subgroup evaluation, and the paired answers can be used to construct preference examples.

title: EchoAlign: Echocardiography foundation model with multilevel report alignment
desc: Echocardiography assesses the structure and function of the heart. Cardiologists read each study across several standard views and report the findings visible in those views by cardiac structure. AI foundation models can learn to analyze these studies from clinical reports, reducing annotation burden and supporting clinical interpretation. However, existing models are trained by pairing each video with the full clinical report, including structures and findings its view does not show. This mismatch lets a model associate a finding with incidental or spurious signals rather than its visual evidence, which limits accuracy, anatomical grounding and clinical trust. Here we introduce EchoAlign, a vision-language foundation model developed on 2.87 million echocardiographic videos and images from 159 clinical centers. title: Towards Clinically Interpretable Ophthalmic VQA via Spatially-Grounded Lesion Evidence
desc: Visual Question Answering (VQA) holds great promise for clinical support, particularly in ophthalmology, where retinal fundus photography is essential for diagnosis. However, ophthalmic VQA benchmarks primarily emphasize answer accuracy, neglecting the explicit visual evidence necessary for clinical interpretability. In this work, we introduce FundusGround, a new benchmark for clinically interpretable ophthalmic VQA with spatially-grounded lesion evidence. Specifically, we propose a three-stage pipeline that collects 10,719 fundus images with 15,595 image-level meticulously annotated lesions. To ensure anatomical consistency and clinical validity, all lesions are spatially localized using the Early Treatment Diabetic Retinopathy Study (ETDRS) grid, enabling standardized mapping to nine clinically meaningful retinal regions. title: A Multi-Center Dataset and Benchmark for SYNTAX Segmentation of Coronary Angiograms
desc: Dense pixel-level classification of coronary angiography is essential for automated cardiovascular diagnostics, yet the computer vision community lacks gold-standard protocols and robust datasets to tackle this topologically complex, heavily long-tailed domain. To bridge this gap, we introduce CARDIAG: a rigorous, multi-center benchmark dataset designed to evaluate deep learning architectures on fine-grained SYNTAX segment classification. Unlike prior efforts, CARDIAG systematically prevents patient- and center-level data leakage while providing an unprecedented suite of annotations: highly imbalanced multi-class labels, explicit catheter and stenosis masks, expert uncertainty maps, temporal sequence frames, and spatial metadata. title: LUCA: A Synthetic World for Experimental Reasoning
desc: An experimental agent can succeed for the wrong reasons. Evaluations, however, often focus on the outcome, not the experiments, evidence, and inferences that produced it. We introduce LUCA, a configurable synthetic world for evaluating this process under fully known ground truth. Agents learn unknown regulatory systems through budgeted experimentation, then predict unseen interventions, diagnose hidden faults, and attempt rescues. This setup allows us to evaluate experiment selection, prediction, diagnosis, and intervention separately. Across seven frontier LLMs and three baselines, these capabilities dissociate sharply.
