title: Unsatz: Evaluating Scientific Discovery Without a Given Ansatz
desc: Before a scientist fits any parameter, they must decide what the model contains: which quantities exist, which are hidden, how they interact, and how they are measured. We introduce Unsatz, a benchmark in which an LLM agent must construct the ansatz itself. title: How Does SAM-3 Adapt? Capacity, Update Geometry, and Domain Transfer
desc: Promptable segmentation foundation models are increasingly used in specialized domains, but it remains unclear how SAM-3 should be fine-tuned when adapting it beyond its original training distribution. We study this question by comparing five adaptation families --LoRA, HiRA, KRAdapter, QuanTA, and Full Fine-Tuning-- across five segmentation datasets spanning medical imaging, remote sensing, and dense material segmentation. Across these datasets, compact parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods often match or approach Full Fine-Tuning in DSC and IoU, suggesting that strong in-domain adaptation does not always require updating the full model. title: LingSante-Pulse: Unified Physiological Pretraining through Random-Feature Prediction and Cross-Modal Alignment
desc: Clinical monitoring and wearable devices capture complementary physiological signals, but their partially overlapping modality coverage makes within-signal information and cross-modal relationships difficult to exploit jointly. We introduce LingSante-Pulse, a unified, general-purpose and flexible physiological representation framework that learns from these heterogeneous recordings. A shared, signal-conditioned encoder processes each physical channel independently and supports different numbers and combinations of signals for multimodal assessment and single-sensor inference. Pairwise cross-modal alignment, structured random-feature prediction (RFP) and masked waveform reconstruction jointly learn physiological relationships and preserve informative within-signal structure. title: TrojanMaxxing: One-shotting VLM Backdoors with Weight-Space Programming
desc: Recent work shows that large language models (LLMs) can reason directly about the weights of other neural networks. Given only a natural-language objective, an LLM can inspect a model's weights, understand what they compute, and edit them directly without gradient-based optimization. title: Comparative Performance of Machine Learning Architectures for Fault Detection and Diagnosis in Chemical Processes
desc: Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) is crucial for both maintenance and control in chemical industries, where early fault detection can prevent costly failures and optimize operations. desc: Classical Fault Detection and Diagnosis (FDD) methods, including many data-driven approaches, assume a static normal operating space and interpret deviations from a fixed reference as fault indicators. title: SLP-Bench: Evaluating and Improving Acoustic Claims of Reasoning Audio Language Models on Clinical Speech
desc: Audio language models (ALMs) can answer clinical questions from speech, outperforming baselines built on handcrafted acoustic features. Reasoning ALMs generate a chain of thought that refers to properties of the speaker's voice before predicting. title: TEA-Bench-BR: Can Coding Agents Turn a Branching Clinical Specification into Correct Code?
desc: Coding agents increasingly implement rules written by domain experts, and bugs in such code are silent: it runs and returns a plausible answer. title: ACESO: Cross-Modal Distillation for Wearable-Free Freezing of Gait Detection in Parkinsons Disease
desc: Freezing of Gait (FoG) is a paroxysmal disruption of motor skills and control caused by the progressive decline in the basal ganglia's capacity to produce dopamine. desc: Vision-language models for medical image segmentation often produce masks that conflict with the accompanying text, especially under multi-site/multi-lesion descriptions. title: EgoSurgHands: An Egocentric 3D Hand Pose Dataset & Benchmark for Open Surgery Training
desc: Surgical skill assessment, AR guidance, and robot learning from demonstration all benefit from 3D tracking of the surgeon's hands, yet no surgical dataset offers real egocentric articulated 3D hand pose. We introduce EgoSurgHands, a benchmark for real-captured egocentric hand pose estimation in open surgery training on synthetic pads. title: Interpretable Tissue Architecture Complements Pathology Foundation Models
desc: Tissue architecture provides important information for histopathological assessment, yet its complementary predictive value alongside pathology foundation-model representations remains insufficiently understood. This study investigates whether interpretable measurements of cellular and multicellular tissue organization provide additional predictive information beyond learned representations. title: Stochastic Grouping Conformal Prediction for Effective Subgroup Reliability
desc: Conformal prediction offers a distribution-free coverage guarantee, making it especially attractive for clinical applications. title: When MLLMs miss what humans read: diagnosing and learning to read squint text
desc: Multimodal LLMs can fail to read text embedded in an image's coarse structure, text a human recovers by squinting, and report that no text is present. title: Change the Number, Change the Answer: Assessing Rating Scale Sensitivity in LLM-Based Text Scoring
desc: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used in computational social science to assign scalar scores to social and psychological constructs. title: One state, many questions: Opsis gives a frontier model typed eyes for pathology
desc: A synoptic pathology report is a checklist of questions with fixed answer sets, many composed from others. desc: Self-supervised learning has been increasingly investigated for low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) image denoising, as it alleviates the dependence on paired normal-dose CT (NDCT) data, which are often difficult to obtain. title: Saddle Buckling of a Multicellular Alga Driven by Differential Growth
desc: During development of many simple multicellular organisms there is a complex interplay between cell growth and generation of an extracellular matrix that confers structure. desc: Large language models increasingly receive high-level instructions about roles, values, interests, and communication style.
